answer: Formulas: Make-Up = Evaporation + Blowdown + Drift; evaporation = metered make-up minus metered blowdown; cycles of concentration approx. = make-up volume / blowdown volume. Numbers: systems typically 2-4 cycles, 6+ possible; raising cycles 3 to 6 cuts make-up 20% and blowdown 50%. Also '100 tons' threshold for automated chemical feed and 'cost to treat 1,000 gallons of make-up water' as a vendor metric. No gallons-per-ton figure stated.
quote: Make-Up = Evaporation + Blowdown + Drift" / "Many systems operate at two to four cycles of concentration, while six cycles or more may be possible." / "Increasing cycles from three to six reduces cooling tower make-up water by 20% and cooling tower blowdown by 50%.
where: FEMP BMP #10 web page (overview and operation/maintenance sections)
